title: Daily AI papers — arXiv announcement batch 2026-10-30
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. The ordering is inferred from corroborated indexing and discussion signals, not readership; citation evidence is limited for papers announced this recently.

sections.title: DynaRev: Benchmarking Web Agents under Dynamic Goal Revision
sections.abstract: Introduces a 181-task benchmark that revises web-agent goals at task-defined milestones and finds that five evaluated models often meet only part of the changed requirements.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce DynaRev with additive, override, and runtime-conditioned goal changes, scoring correctness, responsiveness, and efficiency from agent trajectories.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note that tasks are static web tasks, milestone/evaluation decisions rely on imperfect LLM semantic judgments, and meaningful milestones may be hard to identify for tasks with highly diverse successful trajectories.

sections.title: L3G-World: Real-Time Infinite World Generation with Latent 3D Gaussian Memory
sections.abstract: Proposes a video world model that updates a persistent latent 3D Gaussian memory as it generates new views, aiming to preserve spatial consistency while keeping memory growth tied to explored scene extent rather than stream length.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors' L3G memory stores VAE latent features in 3D Gaussians and renders them directly into the video model's latent space; their experiments report improved long-horizon consistency and faster memory operations.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors explicitly note that the current memory is designed mainly for static scenes; moving-object separation, very large explorations, and error propagation remain limitations.

sections.title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers
sections.abstract: Presents SpecSlot, which assigns pixel-space generation tokens distinct spatial and frequency roles so fine detail can be represented without sending every token through global attention.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors' SpecSlot allocates DCT frequency bands to local slots and reserves global attention for low-frequency carriers; in their reported tests it improves FID over a FLOPs-matched JiT control on ImageNet-512 and reduces forward cost relative to JiT-B/8 on DPG-Bench.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is limited to the reported ImageNet and DPG-Bench settings; these results do not establish performance across other image distributions or generation tasks.

sections.title: Don't Lose the Thread: Empowering Long-Horizon LLM Agents with Cognitive Resource Self-Allocation
sections.abstract: Proposes CORAL, which lets an LLM agent checkpoint progress and verified facts, then reset cluttered context to continue long tasks with fewer input tokens.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 42.8% average accuracy for an 8B model on GAIA while using 6–7× fewer input tokens than a ReAct agent, with further evaluations on multi-hop QA and BrowseComp.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported headline result is benchmark-specific and uses an 8B model; the abstract does not establish that the same gains transfer to deployed agents or other model scales.

sections.title: Gym-Anything for Robotics: Scaling physical simulations with digital agents
sections.abstract: Introduces a coding-agent pipeline for constructing and auditing robot simulations, and releases RoboWorld, a 25-simulation benchmark where the best tested frontier models average 0.06 reward on its test tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors use coding agents to build simulations and adversarial audit agents to check them, selecting candidate tasks using U.S. economic and time-use data; the paper reports 25 built simulations out of 120 selected action groups.
sections.unique_caveat: The work evaluates simulations and simulated learning; it does not demonstrate transfer of the full benchmark to physical robots, and only 25 of 120 selected simulation targets are built in this release.

sections.title: Collaborative AI agents for autonomous experimental research with solid-state quantum spins
sections.abstract: Demonstrates LLM-based agents that formulate and challenge a quantum-spin research question, check a prediction computationally, and revise an experiment after detecting measurement drift.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a laboratory workflow where agents assess one another's work, computationally check a derived calibration result, and redesign measurements after a drifting signal made the first experiment inconclusive.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a demonstration on ensembles of solid-state quantum spins and a defined family of microwave pulse sequences; it does not establish general autonomous research capability across fields.

sections.title: Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs
sections.abstract: Gives a theorem about when separately trained JEPAs can align representations across modalities and reports empirical alignment experiments from caption datasets through text associated with 940 million web images.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors prove a Platonic Representation Theorem under stated positive-pair assumptions, argue that next-token prediction supplies poorer alignment views, and report alignment and captioning experiments.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evidence concerns cross-modal representation alignment and selected zero-shot/captioning evaluations; it does not establish general superiority of JEPAs across AI tasks.
